title: Morgan Stanley Analyst Dismisses 43% AMD GPU Forecast Cut
summary:
A lead researcher at Morgan Stanley has clarified that a recent drop in GPU shipment projections for AMD does not alter the firm's overall investment thesis. The adjustment was a "housekeeping" move by the bank's Asia team, led by Howard Kao, involving a substrate forecast that the lead analyst says cannot be accurately tied to actual chip shipments. This change was part of a larger note and does not impact the firm's primary views on the chipmaker, whose CPU growth is expected to surpass 70% next year.

The discrepancy follows a report that slashed the 2026-2030 GPU demand forecast for AMD from 14.1M to 8M units, a 43.3% decrease, including a 75% cut to 0.6M units specifically for 2026. The bank left its forecasts for Nvidia unchanged, fueling market concerns that cloud providers such as Meta, Amazon, and Google are prioritizing their own custom AI silicon over third party hardware. Some observers have questioned the validity of demand modeling that extends beyond 2027.

selectedTweets.text:
Morgan Stanley's actual AMD analyst: 

"Last week, our Asia team, led by Howard Kao, received significant media attention for cutting its AMD substrate forecast. This appeared to be more of a housekeeping adjustment, albeit a large one, to a number that we have zero ability to triangulate to AMD shipments.

This was a separate, independent change published as part of a much larger note, and we do not believe it is impactful to our forecasts.

Our views on AMD have not changed. We see very robust CPU growth, likely well above the 70% that they have guided to for next year, amid very strong industry growth and a superior roadmap."

selectedTweets.bestBit: Google, Meta, and Amazon would all strongly prefer more wafer allocation to their own custom silicon programs rather than wafers go to AMD
selectedTweets.text:
I’ve been saying for awhile now that it’s not a certainty that AMD gets to continue their accelerator program long term

Many AMD proponents will say that AMD will sell all the silicon they can produce, but that’s a false qualification

All useable silicon will be bought ≠ AMD will have the right to build their accelerator program long term

AMD is in a very precarious position. Stuck between the insatiable demand for NVIDIA hardware, and the insatiable demand for custom ASICs. I don’t think its an exaggeration to say that Google, Meta, and Amazon would all strongly prefer more wafer allocation to their own custom silicon programs rather than wafers go to AMD

Ultimately if there isn’t sufficient ‘true’ demand for AMD accelerators, then the program will fall further behind until it no longer makes economic sense to pursue it

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText: AMD ($AMD) faces a 75% cut in CY26 GPU shipment forecasts to 0.6mn units from 2.4mn, according to Morgan Stanley. The bank also reduced AMD's CY27 projection to 1.3mn units from 2.7mn, while holding Nvidia ($NVDA) GPU assumptions steady at 8.1mn units in CY26 and 7.5mn in CY27. This adjustment concentrates high-end package demand into dominant accelerator designs. Long-term projections show AMD GPU volumes reaching 2.1mn units by CY30 compared to 3.2mn in prior estimates, while Nvidia GPU demand stabilizes at 7.2mn units.
